title: How to Set Up a WhatsApp Catalog So Customers Can Check Out Without Leaving the Chat
summary: A setup guide for WhatsApp's native catalog feature: what customers can actually do inside the chat, what still needs an external link, and how to automate the flow around it.
body_markdown:
## **How can I set up a WhatsApp catalog so customers can browse and check out without leaving the chat?**


Start with the catalog itself, inside Meta's own tools, then build the automation around it. The two are separate layers, and conflating them is where most setup guides get vague.


**Layer one: the catalog.** This lives in your WhatsApp Business app or Meta Commerce Manager. You upload products with photos (short videos work too), pricing, and descriptions. Every new item goes through a review before it's visible to customers, usually within a day, so don't plan a product launch around same-minute approval.


**Layer two: the automation.** Once the catalog exists, a flow decides when to surface it. Someone asks about a product, the bot sends the catalog link along with a clarifying question, and the answer routes toward an order instead of leaving the customer to browse unguided.


## **What customers can actually do inside the chat**


Customers can browse your catalog, tap items, and send you a selection. WhatsApp's native "Cart" feature bundles that into one structured message instead of a string of separate texts. All of that happens entirely inside the chat, no app-switching required.


Payment is the part worth being honest about. Native in-chat checkout depends on region and setup, and for a lot of stores the actual payment step still happens through a link you send after the cart comes in, or a manual confirmation. A setup guide that promises "full checkout, every country" is oversimplifying. Build the flow so the handoff from cart to payment is fast and clear, instead of assuming WhatsApp will handle money end-to-end for you.


## **What goes wrong if you skip the basics**


A few things trip up stores that otherwise do everything right.


*Catalog visibility.* You can hide an out-of-stock item without deleting it, which is useful during a stockout, and separately control whether the whole catalog is visible on your business profile. Mix these two up and you end up with either dead links on live posts or a catalog that looks empty during a quiet restock week.


*Review delays.* Products in "pending" aren't broken. They're waiting on Meta's commerce policy review. Plan new-product pushes a day ahead, not an hour.


*The handoff after "Cart" lands.* A cart message arriving in your inbox isn't the end of the job. Someone, or something, still needs to confirm it, send payment instructions, and follow up if it goes quiet. This is the part a flow builder actually earns its keep on.
